summary: Keyword webhook path is correctly wired: subscriber resolve -> read-only waiting_for_reply precedence probe -> error-isolated fan-out dispatch. Cross-file signatures verified (findByChat, dispatchForSubscriber, mongoTemplate.exists, ExecutionStatus.waiting_for_reply.name()). Error-isolation is a local swallow around the keyword block only, leaving the worker's outer try/catch intact. WARN markers are greppable and PII-free. No blocking issues.

findings.title: Connected-bot resolved twice for one keyword firing
findings.detail: dispatchKeyword resolves the subscriber via findByChat, then dispatchForSubscriber internally re-resolves the CONNECTED bot via botRepository. This is one extra Mongo round-trip per plain-text private message.
findings.reason: Intentional by design (tech-spec Decision 2 / Task 4): FunnelEventService is the single owner of bot-pinning and is also called from non-webhook contexts (tag/field/event/EMIT_EVENT). Passing the already-resolved bot would break that encapsulation and the dispatcher's self-contained contract. The cost is one indexed lookup on an already-DB-bound path.

findings.title: telegramBotId param passed to dispatchKeyword but only used for findByChat
findings.detail: dispatchKeyword takes telegramBotId solely to scope the subscriber lookup; the dispatcher re-derives the bot itself.
findings.reason: findByChat is keyed by (projectId, telegramBotId, chatId) — the param is required for the project-scoped subscriber resolution and matches FunnelTriggerServiceImpl's resolution form. Removing it is not possible.

good_practices: Read-only precedence probe uses mongoTemplate.exists(...) — never the destructive updateMulti, exactly as the task warned.
Status literal uses ExecutionStatus.waiting_for_reply.name() (lowercase, Decision 14) so the criteria matches persisted rows.
Local swallow scoped to the keyword block only; the worker's outer try/catch (FAILED + rethrow) is untouched, so a genuine worker fault still surfaces.
WARN/INFO markers (KEYWORD_DISPATCH_ERROR, KEYWORD_SUPPRESSED_WAITING_FOR_REPLY) are greppable and carry ids/codes only — no message text (Decision 16).
